A1.justification: Both PDFs describe the same Universal Sparse Autoencoders study. Their text, equations, tables, figures, and complete appendices are readable and support comparison, including matching relocated and renumbered material.

before.justification: V1 reports original ImageNet experiments on cross-model reconstruction, concept firing, alignment with independently trained SAEs, and activation-maximization visualizations.

after.justification: V2 retains original ImageNet experiments and additionally reports reconstruction, firing, and qualitative transfer results on DTD and CelebA.

M1.justification: The model-specific encoders and decoders, shared sparse representation, randomly selected encoder-decoder updates, and coordinated activation maximization remain unchanged. Sections 3.1–3.3 and Appendix A.1 retain the same procedure and implementation, including the reported L1 reconstruction loss.

E1.justification: V1 evaluates the USAE on ImageNet. V2 adds DTD textures and CelebA faces as evaluation domains for the ImageNet-trained USAE (Appendix A.4), substantially extending coverage to cross-dataset generalization without adding training datasets.

E2.justification: The corresponding concept-consistency comparisons retain independently trained SAEs and the normally sampled random-dictionary baseline. The added domain evaluations examine the same three vision backbones and introduce no additional competing method.

E3.justification: Appendix A.4 introduces a zero-shot evaluation protocol using the ImageNet-trained USAE on DTD and CelebA validation data. Table 1 additionally reports MSE alongside R2. The existing ImageNet split, dictionary size, preprocessing, and training settings remain unchanged; no protocol change is stated for the revised top-1,000 analysis.

E4.justification: V2 adds substantial distribution-shift testing: reconstruction measurements, firing-entropy and co-firing analyses, and matched concept visualizations across ImageNet, DTD, and CelebA (Table 1 and Figures 13–15). The top-1,000 co-firing consistency analysis is also revised. The DinoV2 unique-concept analysis in new Section 4.6 largely relocates existing appendix material.

E5.justification: Neither version reports repeated-run counts, seeds, confidence intervals, or significance tests for its experiments. V2 extends the existing correlation-reporting practice to additional datasets without introducing a new uncertainty-estimation procedure.

E6.justification: For the reported top-1,000 co-firing comparison, AUCs change from 0.30/0.36/0.40 for SigLIP/DinoV2/ViT in v1 Figure 14 to 0.40/0.65/0.52 in v2 Figure 16, reversing the leading model from ViT to DinoV2. V2 also adds OOD reconstruction, firing, and qualitative results. The main ImageNet reconstruction matrix and full-dictionary consistency scores remain unchanged. The PDFs do not explain the cause of the revised subset scores.

T1.justification: Equations 1–14 retain the same method, objectives, energy definition, reconstruction metric, and firing metrics. No theorem, proof, formal assumption, or substantive mathematical derivation is added or revised.

C1.justification: The abstract, contribution statement, and conclusion retain the same central claims: learning an interpretable shared concept space, identifying universal and model-specific concepts, and enabling coordinated activation maximization. Added domain evaluations support these claims without redefining the stated contributions.

C2.justification: V1 says the top-1,000 subset preserves the overall consistency pattern and emphasizes ViT's strongest overlap. V2 instead interprets this subset as substantially more consistent with independent SAEs, emphasizes DinoV2's stronger representation, and attributes SigLIP's smaller overlap to its image-language space. Appendix A.4 also adds an explicit interpretation of transfer beyond the USAE's training distribution. The existing limitations are retained.

D1.justification: V2 adds a project-page link in Figure 1 and an explicit repository URL for the timm dependency. Appendix A.1 otherwise retains the same optimizer, learning-rate schedule, activation standardization, token alignment, hardware, and training-time disclosures. The PDFs alone do not establish the linked project's contents.

R1.justification: V2 adds discussion of Moschella et al.'s relative representations and Gandelsman et al.'s text-based CLIP decomposition, plus citations to Kowal et al. (2025), DTD, and CelebA. Its positioning against post-hoc concept matching and crosscoders remains intact. Several other reference changes merely update publication metadata.

P1.justification: V2 makes localized introduction and caption edits, promotes the existing DinoV2 analysis into Section 4.6, reorganizes appendix subsections, and adds impact and acknowledgement statements. Author affiliations and publication information also change. Most methodological exposition and the overall narrative remain closely matched.

P2.justification: V2 substantially expands the visual presentation with Table 1 and three new multipanel OOD figures. It combines and condenses v1 Figures 9–10 into main-text Figure 9, reorganizes appendix figures, and redraws the top-1,000 consistency plot with revised curves and caption. Most main-text displays retain their original content.

improvement.justification: The DTD and CelebA evaluations provide useful direct evidence that an ImageNet-trained USAE transfers to other image domains, strengthening a generalization argument previously supported only within ImageNet. The project link also improves access information. However, the substantial revision of the top-1,000 consistency results is unexplained, so it cannot confidently be treated as a correction or quality gain. Overall, the added validation supports a positive but bounded improvement.
